filters.name: Cut mesh along crease edges
filters.shortDescription: Split the mesh along sharp edges.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Cut the mesh along crease edges, duplicating the vertices as necessary. Crease (or sharp) edges are defined according to the variation of normal of the adjacent faces.

parameters.label: Crease Angle (degree)
parameters.help: If the angle between adjacent face normals is larger than this threshold, the edge is treated as a crease and the mesh is cut along it.

filters.name: Laplacian Smooth
filters.shortDescription: Average vertex positions with their neighbors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Laplacian smooth. Average each vertex position with weighted positions of neighbour vertices.
Laplacian Mesh Processing by Olga Sorkine. EUROGRAPHICS 2005
doi:10.2312/egst.20051044

parameters.label: Smoothing steps
parameters.help: Number of smoothing iterations.

parameters.label: 1D Boundary Smoothing
parameters.help: Smooth boundary edges only by themselves instead of shrinking them into the surface.

parameters.label: Cotangent weighting
parameters.help: Use cotangent weights instead of umbrella weights for the position average.

parameters.label: Affect only selection
parameters.help: If enabled, apply the filter only to the selected area.

filters.name: HC Laplacian Smooth
filters.shortDescription: Improved Laplacian smoothing with better shape preservation.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
HC Laplacian Smoothing. Extended version of Laplacian Smoothing based on the article:
Improved Laplacian Smoothing of Noisy Surface Meshes by Vollmer, Mencl and Müller. EUROGRAPHICS Volume 18 (1999), Number 3, 131-138.
doi:10.1111/1467-8659.00334

filters.name: ScaleDependent Laplacian Smooth
filters.shortDescription: Fujiwara-style scale-dependent Laplacian smoothing.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Scale Dependent Laplacian Smoothing, extended version of Laplacian Smoothing based on the Fujiwara extended umbrella operator.
Implicit Fairing of Irregular Meshes using Diffusion and Curvature Flow by Desbrun, Meyer, Schroeder and Barr. SIGGRAPH 1999
doi:10.1145/311535.311576

parameters.label: Smoothing steps
parameters.help: Number of smoothing iterations.

parameters.label: delta
parameters.help: Maximum displacement scale used by the Fujiwara operator.

parameters.label: Affect only selected faces
parameters.help: If enabled, apply the filter only to the selected area.

filters.name: TwoStep Smooth
filters.shortDescription: Feature-preserving smoothing through normal smoothing and vertex fitting.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Two Steps Smoothing, a feature preserving/enhancing fairing filter based on two stages:
  1. Normal Smoothing, where similar normals are averaged together.
  2. Vertex reposition, where vertices are moved to fit on the new normals.
A Comparison of Mesh Smoothing Methods by A. Belyaev and Y. Ohtake. Proc. Israel-Korea Bi-National Conf. Geometric Modeling and Computer Graphics, pp. 83-87, 2003.
publication

parameters.label: Smoothing steps
parameters.help: Number of full algorithm iterations.

parameters.label: Feature Angle Threshold (deg)
parameters.help: Features forming angles larger than this threshold are preserved.

parameters.label: Normal Smoothing steps
parameters.help: Number of normal smoothing iterations per step.

parameters.label: Vertex Fitting steps
parameters.help: Number of vertex fitting iterations per step.

parameters.label: Affect only selected faces
parameters.help: If enabled, perform the filter only on selected faces.

filters.name: Taubin Smooth
filters.shortDescription: Lambda-mu smoothing with reduced shrinkage.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
The λ-μ Taubin smoothing, combines two steps of low-pass filtering for each iteration. Based on the article:
A signal processing approach to fair surface design by Gabriel Taubin, SIGGRAPH 1995
doi:10.1145/218380.218473

parameters.label: Lambda
parameters.help: Lambda parameter of Taubin smoothing.

parameters.label: mu
parameters.help: Mu parameter of Taubin smoothing.

parameters.label: Smoothing steps
parameters.help: Number of Taubin smoothing iterations.

parameters.label: Affect only selected faces
parameters.help: If enabled, apply the filter only to the selected area.

filters.name: Depth Smooth
filters.shortDescription: Smooth vertices only along a given depth direction.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: A laplacian smooth that is constrained to move vertices only in one given direction (usually the viewer direction).

parameters.label: Smoothing steps
parameters.help: Number of smoothing iterations.

parameters.label: Viewpoint
parameters.help: Position of the viewpoint that defines the allowed displacement direction.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.help: How much smoothing is applied: 0 means no smoothing, 1 means full smoothing.

parameters.label: Affect only selection
parameters.help: If enabled, apply the filter only to the selected area.

filters.name: Directional Geometry Preservation
filters.shortDescription: Project smoothed geometry back along a line of sight.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Blend through a given direction the geometry previously stored in a per vertex custom point attribute with the current geometry. This is useful to limit the influence of any smoothing algorithm along the viewing direction. This is useful to cope with the biased distribution of measuring error in many scanning devices, because TOF scanners usually have very good x,y accuracy but suffer of greater depth errors.

parameters.label: Custom attribute name
parameters.help: Name of the per-vertex custom point attribute containing the original geometry.

parameters.label: Viewpoint
parameters.help: Position of the viewpoint used for the directional projection.

filters.name: Smooth Vertex Quality
filters.shortDescription: Laplacian smoothing of vertex quality values.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Laplacian smooth of the quality per vertex values.

filters.name: Smooth Face Normals
filters.shortDescription: Laplacian smoothing of face normals.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Laplacian smooth of the face normals, without touching the position of the vertices.

filters.name: UnSharp Mask Normals
filters.shortDescription: Enhance face normal variation using an unsharp mask.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Unsharp mask filtering of the normals per face, putting in more evidence normal variations.
A simple normal enhancement technique for interactive non-photorealistic renderings by Cignoni, Scopigno and Tarini, Comput Graph, 29 (1) (2005)
doi:10.1016/j.cag.2004.11.012

parameters.label: Recompute Normals

parameters.label: Smooth Iterations

filters.name: UnSharp Mask Geometry
filters.shortDescription: Enhance geometric ridges and valleys with an unsharp mask.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Apply Unsharp filter to geometric shape, putting in more evidence ridges and valleys variations.
Unsharp Masking

parameters.label: Unsharp Weight

filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Apply Unsharp filter to values of quality per vertex.
See Unsharp Masking

parameters.label: Unsharp Weight
parameters.help: Unsharp weight applied to the high-frequency quality component.

parameters.label: Original Weight
parameters.help: Weight of the original quality signal.

parameters.label: Smooth Iterations

filters.name: Re-Compute Vertex Normals
filters.shortDescription: Recompute vertex normals using one of several weighting schemes.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Recompute vertex normals according to four different schemes:
1) Simple (no weights) average of normals of the incident faces
2) Area weighted average of normals of the incident faces
3) Angle weighted sum of normals of the incident faces according to the article [1]. Probably this is the best all-purpose choice. It could slightly bias the result for degenerate, fat triangles.
4) Weighted sum of normals of the incident faces, as defined by article [2]. The weight for each wedge is the cross product of the two edges over the product of the square of the two edge lengths.According to the original article it is perfect only for spherical surface, but it should perform well also in practice.
[1]: Computing Vertex Normals from Polygonal Facet by G Thurmer and CA Wuthrich, JGT volume3, num 1. 1998
doi:10.1080/10867651.1998.10487487
[2]: Weights for Computing Vertex Normals from Facet Normals by Nelson Max, JGT vol4, num 2. 1999
doi:10.1080/10867651.1999.10487501

parameters.label: Weighting Mode
parameters.help: Choose how incident face normals contribute to each vertex normal.

filters.name: Re-Compute Face Normals
filters.shortDescription: Recompute face normals from geometry.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Recompute face normals as the normal of the plane of the face.
See How to find surface normal of a triangle

filters.name: Re-Compute Per-Polygon Face Normals
filters.shortDescription: Recompute polygon-shading normals for faux-edge polygon meshes.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Recompute face normals as the average of the normals of the triangles that builds a polygon. Useful for showing uniformly shaded quad or polygonal meshes represented using faux edges.

filters.name: Normalize Face Normals
filters.shortDescription: Normalize face normals to unit length.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Normalize Face Normal Lengths to unit vectors.

filters.name: Normalize Vertex Normals
filters.shortDescription: Normalize vertex normals to unit length.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Normalize Vertex Normal Lengths to unit vectors.

filters.name: Vertex Linear Morphing
filters.shortDescription: Linearly morph the current mesh toward another mesh.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Morph deformation of current mesh towards a target mesh with the same number of vertices and same vertex ordering. Each vertex of the source mesh is linearly interpolated towards the corresponding vertex on the target mesh using the formula:

resulti = (1-λ)*sourcei + λ*targeti

Three-dimensional metamorphosis: a survey
by F. Lazarus and A. Verroust, Visual Computer, 1998
doi:10.1007/s003710050149

parameters.label: Target Mesh
parameters.help: Mesh that acts as the morph target.

parameters.label: % Morph
parameters.help: 0 keeps the current mesh, 100 reaches the target mesh, values outside [0,100] extrapolate.

filters.name: Generate Scalar Harmonic Field
filters.shortDescription: Compute a harmonic scalar field over the mesh.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Generates a scalar harmonic field over the mesh. Input scalar values must be assigned to two vertices as Dirichlet boundary conditions. Applying the filter, a discrete Laplace operator generates the harmonic field values for all the mesh vertices, which are stored in the quality per vertex attribute of the mesh.
For more details see:Dynamic Harmonic Fields for Surface Processing by Kai Xua, Hao Zhang, Daniel Cohen-Or, Yueshan Xionga. Computers & Graphics, 2009
doi:10.1016/j.cag.2009.03.022

parameters.label: Point 1
parameters.help: A vertex on the mesh representing one harmonic field boundary condition.

parameters.label: Point 2
parameters.help: A vertex on the mesh representing the other harmonic field boundary condition.

parameters.label: value for the 1st point
parameters.help: Harmonic field value assigned to the first constrained vertex.

parameters.label: value for the 2nd point
parameters.help: Harmonic field value assigned to the second constrained vertex.

parameters.label: Also Bake To Color
parameters.help: Also write a per-vertex color ramp after computing the harmonic field. Disabled by default because QMeshLab automatically switches to vertex-quality visualization.
